classReportsV2.title: Present Simple, short answers, frequency and modeled advice
evidence: First attempt 'I playing games' is immediately recast to 'I play games'.
Controlled direct production includes 'I play volleyball' and 'She plays games'.
Repeated guided short answers include 'Yes, I do' and 'No, I don't'.
Negative transformation work exposes unstable do/does and third-person/base-form control.
'I sometimes eat pizza' is produced in a frequency-adverb drill; should/shouldn't output is largely modeled.
classReportsV2.signal: Controlled Present Simple affirmative and short-answer forms are more available than third-person negative auxiliary control; frequency/advice language is strongly scaffolded.
classReportsV2.interpretation: Use low-support first-attempt tasks to separate independent retrieval from successful immediate uptake after recast/model.
classReportsV2.boundary: Tactiq ASR is severely noisy and the lesson is highly guided. Same-turn correction/repetition does not establish mastery.
classReportsV2.nextVerification: Two affirmatives, two negatives contrasting I/you with he/she, two do/does questions, one frequency sentence and one advice sentence without a model.

classReportsV2.title: Economic sectors: classification stronger than explanation
evidence: Agriculture and forestry are retrieved in structured Geography work.
Service examples include firefighter; selected sector classifications are correctly produced in controlled tasks.
Explanation of extractivism/natural-resource use requires substantial teacher scaffolding and is heavily affected by ASR noise.
classReportsV2.signal: Some concrete economic-sector categories and vocabulary are accessible in structured tasks, while independent explanatory language is substantially less stable.
classReportsV2.interpretation: Track sector categorization separately from the ability to explain why an activity belongs to that sector.
classReportsV2.boundary: Severe ASR noise and narrowed-choice prompting prevent a retention or mastery claim.
classReportsV2.nextVerification: Classify three fresh examples with no answer choices and explain each reason in one complete English sentence.

classReportsV2.title: Geography continuity: recognition/classification versus explanation
evidence: Primary/secondary/tertiary classifications recur in structured tasks.
'Opportunity' is retrieved in a push/pull-factor context.
Migration/environment items are often answered through multiple choice or strong prompting; explanation remains more scaffolded.
classReportsV2.signal: Economic-sector concepts remain available across the July 6 to July 8 sequence under structured conditions, but recognition/classification is stronger than independent explanation.
classReportsV2.interpretation: Require a one-sentence reason after each category choice so continuity is not mistaken for measured progress.
classReportsV2.boundary: Continuity across lessons does not itself prove improvement; Tactiq ASR remains severely noisy.
classReportsV2.nextVerification: Use unseen sector and migration/environment examples requiring both answer and reason without a model.

classReportsV2.title: Written-answer difficulty and Geography concept reasoning
evidence: Eduarda directly reports that Geography was harder because it was based on written responses; this is self-report, not a verified school result.
Primary-sector explanation shows partial conceptual confusion that is explicitly repaired by the teacher.
Water-cycle reasoning appears in learner-generated Portuguese explanations even when English lexical formulation is incomplete.
A connected English answer about water importance is assembled with scaffolding, and a Water Cycle sequence is retrieved after rehearsal.
classReportsV2.signal: Relevant Geography concept knowledge can be stronger than independent English formulation; complete written/oral answer production is a material support need.
classReportsV2.interpretation: Preserve content knowledge and English-expression control as separate evidence layers in bilingual school support.
classReportsV2.boundary: No school grade is available; learner self-report and teacher-supported formulation do not establish independent assessment performance.
classReportsV2.nextVerification: Ask two no-model Geography questions, capture the complete English first attempt, and permit a separate Portuguese concept response if English blocks content demonstration.

classReportsV2.title: Water Cycle consolidation under repeated support
evidence: Evaporation, precipitation and sequence language are practiced through repeated elicitation/modeling.
Advanced terms such as transpiration, sublimation, percolation/deposition and runoff are repeatedly rehearsed; most are not independently introduced by the learner.
Several Water Cycle terms become available by lesson end with prompts/corrections.
classReportsV2.signal: Repeated review supports same-lesson availability of Water Cycle terminology and sequence fragments, while advanced vocabulary remains cue-dependent.
classReportsV2.interpretation: Treat this as a consolidation trace and test what survives after a delay without visual/text/model support.
classReportsV2.boundary: Reading/repetition is not spontaneous formulation; same-lesson supported availability is not delayed retention.
classReportsV2.nextVerification: Later, elicit a no-model Water Cycle sequence and two term-to-function explanations before any cue.

classReportsV2.title: Modal language present; function and word order remain uneven
evidence: Controlled ability language includes 'I can speak English'.
'I can make cakes' follows modeling and is followed by the personalized 'I can make tapioca'.
First attempt 'can you I play soccer?' is recast to 'Can you play soccer?', directly exposing question-word-order instability.
should/shouldn't is available with support, but semantic selection is inconsistent in some advice contexts.
A can-to-should correction in an advice task shows functional selection improves after explicit contrast.
classReportsV2.signal: can/can't and should/shouldn't are available in guided production, while functional selection, question word order and complete independent formulation remain unstable.
classReportsV2.interpretation: Do not label modals as absent; test function choice and sentence form separately in student-authored no-model responses.
classReportsV2.boundary: Repeated short answers and modeled sentences do not establish generalized independent modal control.
classReportsV2.nextVerification: One ability statement, one permission question, one advice statement, one can-question and one frequency sentence without stems.

classReportsV2.title: First-attempt evidence strengthens complete-formulation priority
evidence: Direct first attempt 'I can I play volleyball' shows can-sentence word-order instability.
A personalized classroom-rule sentence is produced under support.
First attempt 'I always I go to volleyball...' is reformulated by the teacher, exposing frequency-adverb sentence-organization instability.
'I never drink coffee' is correctly reconstructed in a controlled jumbled-sentence task.
A test-preparation should-response begins as a relevant but incomplete/unstable formulation before teacher reformulation.
classReportsV2.signal: Across the August 19 to 20 sequence, modal/frequency language is available, while independent complete-sentence organization and word order remain a recurring verification target.
classReportsV2.interpretation: Make first-attempt capture the default so teacher-supported final answers do not erase the learner's actual starting point.
classReportsV2.boundary: Consecutive-day continuity is not delayed retention; supplied reading is not spontaneous production.
classReportsV2.nextVerification: Use new no-model modal/frequency prompts plus one complete Geography answer, recording first attempt, self-correction and supported final form separately.
